title: Three Nights and One Short Chair
subtitle: 服务职业 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 服务职业（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·服务行业与职业）
meta: 主题语境：服务职业（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·服务行业与职业）　|　核心词汇：host　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 host 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1979 the guest ① greeted the host that no waiter in the restaurant would have described, and he said the greeting was the whole of the night. The ② host, meaning the welcome itself and not the chair, ran three nights and stayed undescribed in the book; a host, he said, is the only thing in a restaurant that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ host in that restaurant had the same short chair beside it, and the ④ host at the far counter, meaning the seat they kept for the children to keep and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A host, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the guest said the describing is the part that fills three nights.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the host was the whole of the matter, meaning the duty and not the welcome. The ⑥ host, meaning the duty and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; host, he said, is either something you greet or the only word that means both a welcome and a duty. He said the duty is the part they remember.

By 1984 the ⑦ host had become a line in a menu, and the menu had become an argument about the short chair. The ⑧ host of the whole thing, the guest wrote in May, was one restaurant and three nights of describing; host, he said, is either the seat at the far counter or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ host I remember is the welcome described in the menu, which closed in 1986 and is still described as the quietest in the restaurant. A ⑩ host, my mother said in 1988, is the only welcome that improves by being described; every host, she said, is a duty that has agreed to look like a welcome. She said the duty was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 主人；东道主（指餐厅里每一位旁边的那一位）
B. n. 主人；东道主（指那位接待本身，与座椅相对）
C. 固定搭配：greet the host 迎接这位主人
D. n. 主人；东道主（指留给孩子们留的那一个那一位）
E. n. 待客之事（抽象总称，指一处餐厅的主人之事）
F. n. 主人；东道主（指菜单里写到、被记下的的那一位）
G. n. 本分、款待（指一件事里人人都招待却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 款待（抽象总称，指人人都招待却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: greeted the host that no waiter in the restaurant would have described
The host, meaning the welcome itself and not the chair
the host at the far counter
the host was the whole of the matter
the host had become a line in a menu
The host of the whole thing
A host, my mother said in 1988

answers.why: greet the host 意为“迎接这位主人”，1979 年那位客人把餐厅里没有一位侍者肯描述的一位主人做了一遍。
host 意为“主人；东道主”，指那位接待本身而不是座椅，它经过了三个夜而在簿子上没有被描述。
host 意为“主人；东道主”，指餐厅里每一位旁边的那一位，每一位旁边都有同一把小小的座椅。
host 意为“主人；东道主”，指最远那段柜台留给孩子们留的那一个那一位，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
host 意为“本分、款待”，指一件事里人人都招待却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份本分就是那件事的全部。
host 意为“款待”，指人人都招待却无人提起的那样东西而不是那位接待，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
host 意为“主人；东道主”，指菜单里写到、被记下的的那一位，到 1984 年这一位成了菜单里的一行。
host 意为“待客之事”，客人五月写道，整件事的主人之事是一处餐厅和三个夜的描述。
host 意为“主人；东道主”，我记得的是菜单里描述过的那一位，1986 年歇业了，至今仍被说成餐厅里最安静的一位。
host 为抽象总称，母亲 1988 年说，主人是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的接待。
